    13	/// Register with a simple stream-like ready/valid handshake.
    14	/// This register does not cut combinatorial paths on all control signals; if you need a complete
    15	/// cut, use the `spill_register`.
    16	module stream_register #(
    17	    parameter type T = logic  // Vivado requires a default value for type parameters.
    18	) (
    19	    input  logic    clk_i,          // Clock
    20	    input  logic    rst_ni,         // Asynchronous active-low reset
    21	    input  logic    clr_i,          // Synchronous clear
    22	    input  logic    testmode_i,     // Test mode to bypass clock gating
    23	    // Input port
    24	    input  logic    valid_i,
    25	    output logic    ready_o,
    26	    input  T        data_i,
    27	    // Output port
    28	    output logic    valid_o,
    29	    input  logic    ready_i,
    30	    output T        data_o
    31	);
    32	
    33	    logic reg_ena;
    34	    assign ready_o = ready_i | ~valid_o;
    35	    assign reg_ena = valid_i & ready_o;
    36	    // Load-enable FFs with synch clear
    37	    `FFLARNC(valid_o, valid_i, ready_o, clr_i, 1'b0  , clk_i, rst_ni)
    38	    `FFLARNC(data_o,   data_i, reg_ena, clr_i, T'('0), clk_i, rst_ni)
    39	
    40	endmodule

    15	module fifo_v3 #(
    16	    parameter bit          FALL_THROUGH = 1'b0, // fifo is in fall-through mode
    17	    parameter int unsigned DATA_WIDTH   = 32,   // default data width if the fifo is of type logic
    18	    parameter int unsigned DEPTH        = 8,    // depth can be arbitrary from 0 to 2**32
    19	    parameter type dtype                = logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0],
    20	    // DO NOT OVERWRITE THIS PARAMETER
    21	    parameter int unsigned ADDR_DEPTH   = (DEPTH > 1) ? $clog2(DEPTH) : 1
    22	)(
    23	    input  logic  clk_i,            // Clock
    24	    input  logic  rst_ni,           // Asynchronous reset active low
    25	    input  logic  flush_i,          // flush the queue
    26	    input  logic  testmode_i,       // test_mode to bypass clock gating
    27	    // status flags
    28	    output logic  full_o,           // queue is full
    29	    output logic  empty_o,          // queue is empty
    30	    output logic  [ADDR_DEPTH-1:0] usage_o,  // fill pointer
    31	    // as long as the queue is not full we can push new data
    32	    input  dtype  data_i,           // data to push into the queue
    33	    input  logic  push_i,           // data is valid and can be pushed to the queue
    34	    // as long as the queue is not empty we can pop new elements
    35	    output dtype  data_o,           // output data
    36	    input  logic  pop_i             // pop head from queue
    37	);
    38	    // local parameter
    39	    // FIFO depth - handle the case of pass-through, synthesizer will do constant propagation
    40	    localparam int unsigned FifoDepth = (DEPTH > 0) ? DEPTH : 1;
    41	    // clock gating control
    42	    logic gate_clock;
    43	    // pointer to the read and write section of the queue
    44	    logic [ADDR_DEPTH - 1:0] read_pointer_n, read_pointer_q, write_pointer_n, write_pointer_q;
    45	    // keep a counter to keep track of the current queue status
    46	    // this integer will be truncated by the synthesis tool
    47	    logic [ADDR_DEPTH:0] status_cnt_n, status_cnt_q;
    48	    // actual memory
    49	    dtype [FifoDepth - 1:0] mem_n, mem_q;
    50	
    51	    assign usage_o = status_cnt_q[ADDR_DEPTH-1:0];
    52	
    53	    if (DEPTH == 0) begin : gen_pass_through
    54	        assign empty_o     = ~push_i;
    55	        assign full_o      = ~pop_i;
    56	    end else begin : gen_fifo
    57	        assign full_o       = (status_cnt_q == FifoDepth[ADDR_DEPTH:0]);
    58	        assign empty_o      = (status_cnt_q == 0) & ~(FALL_THROUGH & push_i);
    59	    end
    60	    // status flags
    61	
    62	    // read and write queue logic
    63	    always_comb begin : read_write_comb
    64	        // default assignment
    65	        read_pointer_n  = read_pointer_q;
    66	        write_pointer_n = write_pointer_q;
    67	        status_cnt_n    = status_cnt_q;
    68	        data_o          = (DEPTH == 0) ? data_i : mem_q[read_pointer_q];
    69	        mem_n           = mem_q;
    70	        gate_clock      = 1'b1;
    71	
    72	        // push a new element to the queue
    73	        if (push_i && ~full_o) begin
    74	            // push the data onto the queue
    75	            mem_n[write_pointer_q] = data_i;
    76	            // un-gate the clock, we want to write something
    77	            gate_clock = 1'b0;
    78	            // increment the write counter
    79	            // this is dead code when DEPTH is a power of two
    80	            if (write_pointer_q == FifoDepth[ADDR_DEPTH-1:0] - 1)
    81	                write_pointer_n = '0;
    82	            else
    83	                write_pointer_n = write_pointer_q + 1;
    84	            // increment the overall counter
    85	            status_cnt_n    = status_cnt_q + 1;
    86	        end
    87	
    88	        if (pop_i && ~empty_o) begin
    89	            // read from the queue is a default assignment
    90	            // but increment the read pointer...
    91	            // this is dead code when DEPTH is a power of two
    92	            if (read_pointer_n == FifoDepth[ADDR_DEPTH-1:0] - 1)
    93	                read_pointer_n = '0;
    94	            else
    95	                read_pointer_n = read_pointer_q + 1;
    96	            // ... and decrement the overall count
    97	            status_cnt_n   = status_cnt_q - 1;
    98	        end
    99	
   100	        // keep the count pointer stable if we push and pop at the same time
   101	        if (push_i && pop_i &&  ~full_o && ~empty_o)
   102	            status_cnt_n   = status_cnt_q;
   103	
   104	        // FIFO is in pass through mode -> do not change the pointers
   105	        if (FALL_THROUGH && (status_cnt_q == 0) && push_i) begin
   106	            data_o = data_i;
   107	            if (pop_i) begin
   108	                status_cnt_n = status_cnt_q;
   109	                read_pointer_n = read_pointer_q;
   110	                write_pointer_n = write_pointer_q;
   111	            end
   112	        end
   113	    end
   114	
   115	    // sequential process
   116	    always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
   117	        if(~rst_ni) begin
   118	            read_pointer_q  <= '0;
   119	            write_pointer_q <= '0;
   120	            status_cnt_q    <= '0;
   121	        end else begin
   122	            if (flush_i) begin
   123	                read_pointer_q  <= '0;
   124	                write_pointer_q <= '0;
   125	                status_cnt_q    <= '0;
   126	             end else begin
   127	                read_pointer_q  <= read_pointer_n;
   128	                write_pointer_q <= write_pointer_n;
   129	                status_cnt_q    <= status_cnt_n;
   130	            end
   131	        end
   132	    end
   133	
   134	    always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
   135	        if(~rst_ni) begin
   136	            mem_q <= {FifoDepth{dtype'('0)}};
   137	        end else if (!gate_clock) begin
   138	            mem_q <= mem_n;
   139	        end
   140	    end
   141	
   142	`ifndef COMMON_CELLS_ASSERTS_OFF
   143	    `ASSERT_INIT(depth_0, DEPTH > 0, "DEPTH must be greater than 0.")
   144	
   145	    `ASSERT(full_write, full_o |-> ~push_i, clk_i, !rst_ni,
   146	            "Trying to push new data although the FIFO is full.")
   147	
   148	    `ASSERT(empty_read, empty_o |-> ~pop_i, clk_i, !rst_ni,
   149	            "Trying to pop data although the FIFO is empty.")
   150	`endif
   151	
   152	endmodule // fifo_v3

    13	/// Stream multiplexer: connects the output to one of `N_INP` data streams with valid-ready
    14	/// handshaking.
    15	
    16	module stream_mux #(
    17	  parameter type DATA_T = logic,  // Vivado requires a default value for type parameters.
    18	  parameter integer N_INP = 0,    // Synopsys DC requires a default value for value parameters.
    19	  /// Dependent parameters, DO NOT OVERRIDE!
    20	  parameter integer SEL_WIDTH = cf_math_pkg::idx_width(N_INP)
    21	) (
    22	  input  DATA_T [N_INP-1:0]     inp_data_i,
    23	  input  logic  [N_INP-1:0]     inp_valid_i,
    24	  output logic  [N_INP-1:0]     inp_ready_o,
    25	
    26	  input  logic  [SEL_WIDTH-1:0] inp_sel_i,
    27	
    28	  output DATA_T                 oup_data_o,
    29	  output logic                  oup_valid_o,
    30	  input  logic                  oup_ready_i
    31	);
    32	
    33	  always_comb begin
    34	    inp_ready_o = '0;
    35	    inp_ready_o[inp_sel_i] = oup_ready_i;
    36	  end
    37	  assign oup_data_o   = inp_data_i[inp_sel_i];
    38	  assign oup_valid_o  = inp_valid_i[inp_sel_i];
    39	
    40	`ifndef COMMON_CELLS_ASSERTS_OFF
    41	  `ASSERT_INIT(n_inp_0, N_INP >= 1, "The number of inputs must be at least 1!")
    42	`endif
    43	
    44	endmodule

    14	// Description: logarithmic arbitration tree with round robin arbitration scheme.

    18	/// The rr_arb_tree employs non-starving round robin-arbitration - i.e., the priorities
    19	/// rotate each cycle.
    20	///
    21	/// ## Fair vs. unfair Arbitration
    22	///
    23	/// This refers to fair throughput distribution when not all inputs have active requests.
    24	/// This module has an internal state `rr_q` which defines the highest priority input. (When
    25	/// `ExtPrio` is `1'b1` this state is provided from the outside.) The arbitration tree will
    26	/// choose the input with the same index as currently defined by the state if it has an active
    27	/// request. Otherwise a *random* other active input is selected. The parameter `FairArb` is used
    28	/// to distinguish between two methods of calculating the next state.
    29	/// * `1'b0`: The next state is calculated by advancing the current state by one. This leads to the
    30	///           state being calculated without the context of the active request. Leading to an
    31	///           unfair throughput distribution if not all inputs have active requests.
    32	/// * `1'b1`: The next state jumps to the next unserved request with higher index.
    33	///           This is achieved by using two trailing-zero-counters (`lzc`). The upper has the masked
    34	///           `req_i` signal with all indices which will have a higher priority in the next state.
    35	///           The trailing zero count defines the input index with the next highest priority after
    36	///           the current one is served. When the upper is empty the lower `lzc` provides the
    37	///           wrapped index if there are outstanding requests with lower or same priority.
    38	/// The implication of throughput fairness on the module timing are:
    39	/// * The trailing zero counter (`lzc`) has a loglog relation of input to output timing. This means
    40	///   that in this module the input to register path scales with Log(Log(`NumIn`)).
    41	/// * The `rr_arb_tree` data multiplexing scales with Log(`NumIn`). This means that the input to output
    42	///   timing path of this module also scales scales with Log(`NumIn`).
    43	/// This implies that in this module the input to output path is always longer than the input to
    44	/// register path. As the output data usually also terminates in a register the parameter `FairArb`
    45	/// only has implications on the area. When it is `1'b0` a static plus one adder is instantiated.
    46	/// If it is `1'b1` two `lzc`, a masking logic stage and a two input multiplexer are instantiated.
    47	/// However these are small in respect of the data multiplexers needed, as the width of the `req_i`
    48	/// signal is usually less as than `DataWidth`.
    49	module rr_arb_tree #(
    50	  /// Number of inputs to be arbitrated.
    51	  parameter int unsigned NumIn      = 64,
    52	  /// Data width of the payload in bits. Not needed if `DataType` is overwritten.
    53	  parameter int unsigned DataWidth  = 32,
    54	  /// Data type of the payload, can be overwritten with custom type. Only use of `DataWidth`.
    55	  parameter type         DataType   = logic [DataWidth-1:0],
    56	  /// The `ExtPrio` option allows to override the internal round robin counter via the
    57	  /// `rr_i` signal. This can be useful in case multiple arbiters need to have
    58	  /// rotating priorities that are operating in lock-step. If static priority arbitration
    59	  /// is needed, just connect `rr_i` to '0.
    60	  ///
    61	  /// Set to 1'b1 to enable.
    62	  parameter bit          ExtPrio    = 1'b0,
    63	  /// If `AxiVldRdy` is set, the req/gnt signals are compliant with the AXI style vld/rdy
    64	  /// handshake. Namely, upstream vld (req) must not depend on rdy (gnt), as it can be deasserted
    65	  /// again even though vld is asserted. Enabling `AxiVldRdy` leads to a reduction of arbiter
    66	  /// delay and area.
    67	  ///
    68	  /// Set to `1'b1` to treat req/gnt as vld/rdy.
    69	  parameter bit          AxiVldRdy  = 1'b0,
    70	  /// The `LockIn` option prevents the arbiter from changing the arbitration
    71	  /// decision when the arbiter is disabled. I.e., the index of the first request
    72	  /// that wins the arbitration will be locked in case the destination is not
    73	  /// able to grant the request in the same cycle.
    74	  ///
    75	  /// Set to `1'b1` to enable.
    76	  parameter bit          LockIn     = 1'b0,
    77	  /// When set, ensures that throughput gets distributed evenly between all inputs.
    78	  ///
    79	  /// Set to `1'b0` to disable.
    80	  parameter bit          FairArb    = 1'b1,
    81	  /// Dependent parameter, do **not** overwrite.
    82	  /// Width of the arbitration priority signal and the arbitrated index.
    83	  parameter int unsigned IdxWidth   = (NumIn > 32'd1) ? unsigned'($clog2(NumIn)) : 32'd1,
    84	  /// Dependent parameter, do **not** overwrite.
    85	  /// Type for defining the arbitration priority and arbitrated index signal.
    86	  parameter type         idx_t      = logic [IdxWidth-1:0]
    87	) (
    88	  /// Clock, positive edge triggered.
    89	  input  logic                clk_i,
    90	  /// Asynchronous reset, active low.
    91	  input  logic                rst_ni,

   181	            if (flush_i) begin

   264	            assign gnt_o[l*2+1]      = gnt_nodes[Idx0] & (AxiVldRdy | req_d[l*2+1]) & sel;
   265	          end
   266	          // if only the first index is still in the vector...

   270	            assign data_nodes[Idx0]  = data_i[l*2];
   271	            assign gnt_o[l*2]        = gnt_nodes[Idx0] & (AxiVldRdy | req_d[l*2]);
   272	          end
   273	          // if index is out of range, fill up with zeros (will get pruned)
   274	          if (unsigned'(l) * 2 > NumIn-1) begin : gen_out_of_range
   275	            assign req_nodes[Idx0]   = 1'b0;
   276	            assign index_nodes[Idx0] = idx_t'('0);
   277	            assign data_nodes[Idx0]  = DataType'('0);
   278	          end
   279	        //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
   280	        // general case for other levels within the tree
   281	        end else begin : gen_other_levels
   282	          assign req_nodes[Idx0]   = req_nodes[Idx1] | req_nodes[Idx1+1];
   283	
   284	          // arbitration: round robin
   285	          assign sel =  ~req_nodes[Idx1] | req_nodes[Idx1+1] & rr_q[NumLevels-1-level];

   287	          assign index_nodes[Idx0] = (sel) ?

   289	            idx_t'({1'b0, index_nodes[Idx1][NumLevels-unsigned'(level)-2:0]});

   291	          assign data_nodes[Idx0]  = (sel) ? data_nodes[Idx1+1] : data_nodes[Idx1];
   292	          assign gnt_nodes[Idx1]   = gnt_nodes[Idx0] & ~sel;
   293	          assign gnt_nodes[Idx1+1] = gnt_nodes[Idx0] & sel;
   294	        end
   295	        //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
   296	      end
   297	    end

   319	  end

   147	    // module under reset flag
   148	    logic under_rst;
   149	    always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
   150	      if (!rst_ni) begin
   151	        under_rst <= 1'b1;
   152	      end else if (under_rst) begin

   154	      end
   155	    end

   157	    logic empty;

   159	    // full and not ready for write are two different concepts.

     4	//
     5	// Hardened counter primitive:
     6	//
     7	// This internally uses a cross counter scheme with primary and a secondary counter, where the
     8	// secondary counter counts in reverse direction. The sum of both counters must remain constant and
     9	// equal to 2**Width-1 or otherwise an err_o will be asserted.
    10	//
    11	// This counter supports a generic clear / set / increment / decrement interface:
    12	//
    13	// clr_i: This clears the primary counter to ResetValue and adjusts the secondary counter to match
    14	//        (i.e. 2**Width-1-ResetValue). Clear has priority over set, increment and decrement.
    15	// set_i: This sets the primary counter to set_cnt_i and adjusts the secondary counter to match
    16	//        (i.e. 2**Width-1-set_cnt_i). Set has priority over increment and decrement.
    17	// incr_en_i: Increments the primary counter by step_i, and decrements the secondary by step_i.
    18	// decr_en_i: Decrements the primary counter by step_i, and increments the secondary by step_i.
    19	// commit_i: Counter changes only take effect when `commit_i` is set. This does not effect the
    20	//           `cnt_after_commit_o` output which gives the next counter state if the change is
    21	//           committed.
    22	//
    23	// Note that if both incr_en_i and decr_en_i are asserted at the same time, the counter remains
    24	// unchanged. The counter is also protected against under- and overflows.
    25	
    26	`include "prim_assert.sv"
    27	
    28	module prim_count
    29	  import prim_count_pkg::*;
    30	#(
    31	  parameter int               Width = 2,
    32	  // Can be used to reset the counter to a different value than 0, for example when
    33	  // the counter is used as a down-counter.
    34	  parameter logic [Width-1:0] ResetValue = '0,
    35	  // This should only be disabled in special circumstances, for example
    36	  // in non-comportable IPs where an error does not trigger an alert.
    37	  parameter bit               EnableAlertTriggerSVA = 1,
    38	
    39	  // We have some assertions below with preconditions that depend on particular input actions
    40	  // (clear, set, incr, decr). If the design has instantiated prim_count with one of these actions
    41	  // tied to zero, the preconditions for the associated assertions will not be satisfiable. The
    42	  // result is an unreachable item, which we treat as a failed assertion in the report.
    43	  //
    44	  // To avoid this, we the instantiation to specify the actions which might happen. If this is not
    45	  // '1, we will have an assertion which assert the corresponding action is never triggered. We can
    46	  // then use this to avoid the unreachable assertions.
    47	  parameter action_mask_t     PossibleActions = {$bits(action_mask_t){1'b1}}
    48	) (
    49	  input clk_i,
    50	  input rst_ni,
    51	  input clr_i,
    52	  input set_i,
    53	  input [Width-1:0] set_cnt_i,                 // Set value for the counter.
    54	  input incr_en_i,
    55	  input decr_en_i,
    56	  input [Width-1:0] step_i,                    // Increment/decrement step when enabled.
    57	  input commit_i,
    58	  output logic [Width-1:0] cnt_o,              // Current counter state
    59	  output logic [Width-1:0] cnt_after_commit_o, // Next counter state if committed
    60	  output logic err_o
    61	);
    62	
    63	  ///////////////////
    64	  // Counter logic //
    65	  ///////////////////
    66	
    67	  // Reset Values for primary and secondary counters.
    68	  localparam int NumCnt = 2;
    69	  localparam logic [NumCnt-1:0][Width-1:0] ResetValues = {{Width{1'b1}} - ResetValue, // secondary
    70	                                                          ResetValue};                // primary
    71	
    72	  logic [NumCnt-1:0][Width-1:0] cnt_d, cnt_d_committed, cnt_q;
    73	
    74	  // The fpv_force signal can be used in FPV runs to make the internal counters (cnt_q) jump
    75	  // unexpectedly. We only want to use this mechanism when we're doing FPV on prim_count itself. In
    76	  // that situation, we will have the PrimCountFpv define and wish to leave fpv_force undriven so
    77	  // that it becomes a free variable in FPV. In any other situation, we drive the signal with zero.
    78	  logic [NumCnt-1:0][Width-1:0] fpv_force;
    79	`ifndef PrimCountFpv
    80	  assign fpv_force = '0;
    81	`endif
    82	
    83	  for (genvar k = 0; k < NumCnt; k++) begin : gen_cnts
    84	    // Note that increments / decrements are reversed for the secondary counter.
    85	    logic incr_en, decr_en;
    86	    logic [Width-1:0] set_val;
    87	    if (k == 0) begin : gen_up_cnt
    88	      assign incr_en = incr_en_i;
    89	      assign decr_en = decr_en_i;
    90	      assign set_val = set_cnt_i;
    91	    end else begin : gen_dn_cnt
    92	      assign incr_en = decr_en_i;
    93	      assign decr_en = incr_en_i;
    94	      // The secondary value needs to be adjusted accordingly.
    95	      assign set_val = {Width{1'b1}} - set_cnt_i;
    96	    end
    97	
    98	    // Main counter logic
    99	    logic [Width:0] ext_cnt;
   100	    assign ext_cnt = (decr_en) ? {1'b0, cnt_q[k]} - {1'b0, step_i} :
   101	                     (incr_en) ? {1'b0, cnt_q[k]} + {1'b0, step_i} : {1'b0, cnt_q[k]};
   102	
   103	    // Saturation logic
   104	    logic uflow, oflow;
   105	    assign oflow = incr_en && ext_cnt[Width];
   106	    assign uflow = decr_en && ext_cnt[Width];
   107	    logic [Width-1:0] cnt_sat;
   108	    assign cnt_sat = (uflow) ? '0            :
   109	                     (oflow) ? {Width{1'b1}} : ext_cnt[Width-1:0];
   110	
   111	    // Clock gate flops when in saturation, and do not
   112	    // count if both incr_en and decr_en are asserted.
   113	    logic cnt_en;
   114	    assign cnt_en = (incr_en ^ decr_en) &&
   115	                    ((incr_en && !(&cnt_q[k])) ||
   116	                    (decr_en && !(cnt_q[k] == '0)));
   117	
   118	    // Counter muxes
   119	    assign cnt_d[k] = (clr_i)  ? ResetValues[k] :
   120	                      (set_i)  ? set_val        :
   121	                      (cnt_en) ? cnt_sat        : cnt_q[k];
   122	
   123	    assign cnt_d_committed[k] = commit_i ? cnt_d[k] : cnt_q[k];
   124	
   125	    logic [Width-1:0] cnt_unforced_q;
   126	    prim_flop #(
   127	      .Width(Width),
   128	      .ResetValue(ResetValues[k])
   129	    ) u_cnt_flop (
   130	      .clk_i,
   131	      .rst_ni,
   132	      .d_i(cnt_d_committed[k]),
   133	      .q_o(cnt_unforced_q)
   134	    );
   135	
   136	    // fpv_force is only used during FPV.
   137	    assign cnt_q[k] = fpv_force[k] + cnt_unforced_q;
   138	  end
   139	
   140	  // The sum of both counters must always equal the counter maximum.
   141	  logic [Width:0] sum;
   142	  assign sum = (cnt_q[0] + cnt_q[1]);
   143	
   144	  // Register the error signal to avoid potential CDC issues downstream.
   145	  logic err_d, err_q;
   146	  assign err_d = (sum != {1'b0, {Width{1'b1}}});
   147	  always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
   148	    if (!rst_ni) begin
   149	      err_q <= 1'b0;
   150	    end else begin
   151	      err_q <= err_d;
   152	    end
   153	  end
   154	  assign err_o = err_q;
   155	
   156	  // Output count values
   157	  assign cnt_o              = cnt_q[0];
   158	  assign cnt_after_commit_o = cnt_d[0];
   159	
   160	  ////////////////
   161	  // Assertions //
   162	  ////////////////
   163	`ifdef INC_ASSERT
   164	  //VCS coverage off
   165	  // pragma coverage off
   166	
   167	  // We need to disable most assertions in that case using a helper signal.
   168	  // We can't rely on err_o since some error patterns cannot be detected (e.g. all error
   169	  // patterns that still fulfil the sum constraint).
   170	  logic fpv_err_present;
   171	  assign fpv_err_present = |fpv_force;
   172	
   173	  // Helper functions for assertions.
   174	  function automatic logic signed [Width+1:0] max(logic signed [Width+1:0] a,
   175	                                                  logic signed [Width+1:0] b);
   176	    return (a > b) ? a : b;
   177	  endfunction
   178	
   179	  function automatic logic signed [Width+1:0] min(logic signed [Width+1:0] a,
   180	                                                  logic signed [Width+1:0] b);
   181	    return (a < b) ? a : b;
   182	  endfunction
   183	  //VCS coverage on
   184	  // pragma coverage on
   185	
   186	  if (!(PossibleActions & Clr)) begin : g_check_no_clr
   187	    `ASSERT(ClrNeverTrue_A, clr_i !== 1'b1)
   188	  end
   189	  if (!(PossibleActions & Set)) begin : g_check_no_set
   190	    `ASSERT(SetNeverTrue_A, set_i !== 1'b1)
   191	  end
   192	  if (!(PossibleActions & Incr)) begin : g_check_no_incr
   193	    `ASSERT(IncrNeverTrue_A, incr_en_i !== 1'b1)
   194	  end
   195	  if (!(PossibleActions & Decr)) begin : g_check_no_decr
   196	    `ASSERT(DecrNeverTrue_A, decr_en_i !== 1'b1)
   197	  end
   198	
   199	  // Cnt next
   200	  `ASSERT(CntNext_A,
   201	      rst_ni
   202	      |=>
   203	      $past(!commit_i) || (cnt_o == $past(cnt_after_commit_o)),
   204	      clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
   205	
   206	  // Clear
   207	  if (PossibleActions & Clr) begin : g_check_clr_fwd_a
   208	    `ASSERT(ClrFwd_A,
   209	            rst_ni && commit_i && clr_i
   210	            |=>
   211	            (cnt_o == ResetValue) &&
   212	            (cnt_q[1] == ({Width{1'b1}} - ResetValue)),
   213	            clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
   214	  end
   215	
   216	  // Set
   217	  if (PossibleActions & Set) begin : g_check_set_fwd_a
   218	    `ASSERT(SetFwd_A,
   219	        rst_ni && commit_i && set_i && !clr_i
   220	        |=>
   221	        (cnt_o == $past(set_cnt_i)) &&
   222	        (cnt_q[1] == ({Width{1'b1}} - $past(set_cnt_i))),
   223	        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
   224	  end
   225	
   226	  // Do not count if both increment and decrement are asserted.
   227	  if ((PossibleActions & Incr) && (PossibleActions & Decr)) begin : g_check_inc_and_dec
   228	    `ASSERT(IncrDecrUpDnCnt_A,
   229	        rst_ni && incr_en_i && decr_en_i && !(clr_i || set_i)
   230	        |=>
   231	        $stable(cnt_o) && $stable(cnt_q[1]),
   232	        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
   233	  end
   234	
   235	  // Increment
   236	  if ((PossibleActions & Incr)) begin : g_check_incr
   237	    `ASSERT(IncrUpCnt_A,
   238	        rst_ni && incr_en_i && !(clr_i || set_i || decr_en_i) && commit_i
   239	        |=>
   240	        cnt_o == min($past(cnt_o) + $past({2'b0, step_i}), {2'b0, {Width{1'b1}}}),
   241	        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
   242	    `ASSERT(IncrDnCnt_A,
   243	        rst_ni && incr_en_i && !(clr_i || set_i || decr_en_i) && commit_i
   244	        |=>
   245	        cnt_q[1] == max($past(signed'({2'b0, cnt_q[1]})) - $past({2'b0, step_i}), '0),
   246	        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
   247	    `ASSERT(UpCntIncrStable_A,
   248	        incr_en_i && !(clr_i || set_i || decr_en_i) &&
   249	        cnt_o == {Width{1'b1}}
   250	        |=>
   251	        $stable(cnt_o),
   252	        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
   253	    `ASSERT(DnCntIncrStable_A,
   254	        rst_ni && incr_en_i && !(clr_i || set_i || decr_en_i) &&
   255	        cnt_q[1] == '0
   256	        |=>
   257	        $stable(cnt_q[1]),
   258	        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
   259	  end
   260	
   261	  // Decrement
   262	  if ((PossibleActions & Decr)) begin : g_check_decr
   263	    `ASSERT(DecrUpCnt_A,
   264	        rst_ni && decr_en_i && !(clr_i || set_i || incr_en_i) && commit_i
   265	        |=>
   266	        cnt_o == max($past(signed'({2'b0, cnt_o})) - $past({2'b0, step_i}), '0),
   267	        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
   268	    `ASSERT(DecrDnCnt_A,
   269	        rst_ni && decr_en_i && !(clr_i || set_i || incr_en_i) && commit_i
   270	        |=>
   271	        cnt_q[1] == min($past(cnt_q[1]) + $past({2'b0, step_i}), {2'b0, {Width{1'b1}}}),
   272	        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
   273	    `ASSERT(UpCntDecrStable_A,
   274	        decr_en_i && !(clr_i || set_i || incr_en_i) &&
   275	        cnt_o == '0
   276	        |=>
   277	        $stable(cnt_o),
   278	        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
   279	    `ASSERT(DnCntDecrStable_A,
   280	        rst_ni && decr_en_i && !(clr_i || set_i || incr_en_i) &&
   281	        cnt_q[1] == {Width{1'b1}}
   282	        |=>
   283	        $stable(cnt_q[1]),
   284	        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
   285	  end
   286	
   287	  // A backwards check for count changes. This asserts that the count only changes if one of the
   288	  // inputs that should tell it to change (clear, set, increment, decrement) does so.
   289	  `ASSERT(ChangeBackward_A,
   290	          rst_ni ##1 $changed(cnt_o) && $changed(cnt_q[1])
   291	          |->
   292	          $past(clr_i || set_i || (commit_i && (incr_en_i || decr_en_i))),
   293	          clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
   294	
   295	  // Check that count errors are reported properly in err_o
   296	  //
   297	  // This is essentially a "|=> implication", but is structured in a way to avoid generating a cover
   298	  // property for the left hand side if PrimCountFpv is not defined (because we won't have a way to
   299	  // inject an error if not)
   300	  `ASSERT(CntErrReported_A, ##1 $past((cnt_q[1] + cnt_q[0]) != {Width{1'b1}}) == err_o)
   301	 `ifdef PrimCountFpv
   302	  `COVER(CntErr_C, err_o)
   303	 `endif
   304	
   305	  // This logic that will be assign to one, when user adds macro
   306	  // ASSERT_PRIM_COUNT_ERROR_TRIGGER_ALERT to check the error with alert, in case that prim_count
   307	  // is used in design without adding this assertion check.
   308	  logic unused_assert_connected;
   309	
   310	  `ASSERT_INIT_NET(AssertConnected_A, unused_assert_connected === 1'b1 || !EnableAlertTriggerSVA)
   311	`endif

    44	module prim_packer_fifo #(
    45	  parameter int InW  = 32,
    46	  parameter int OutW = 8,
    47	  parameter bit ClearOnRead = 1'b1, // if == 1 always output 0 after read
    48	  // derived parameters
    49	  localparam int MaxW = (InW > OutW) ? InW : OutW,
    50	  localparam int MinW = (InW < OutW) ? InW : OutW,
    51	  localparam int DepthW = $clog2(MaxW/MinW)

    53	  input logic clk_i ,
    54	  input logic rst_ni,

    60	
    61	  output logic              rvalid_o,
    62	  output logic [OutW-1:0]   rdata_o,
    63	  input logic               rready_i,
    64	  output logic [DepthW:0]   depth_o
    65	);
    66	
    67	  localparam int unsigned   WidthRatio = MaxW / MinW;
    68	  localparam bit [DepthW:0] FullDepth = WidthRatio[DepthW:0];
    69	  localparam bit [DepthW:0] DepthOne = 1;
    70	
    71	  // signals
    72	  logic  load_data;
    73	  logic  clear_data;
    74	  logic  clear_status;
    75	
    76	  // flops
    77	  logic [DepthW:0] depth_q, depth_d;
    78	  logic [MaxW-1:0] data_q, data_d;
    79	  logic            clr_q, clr_d;
    80	
    81	  always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
    82	    if (!rst_ni) begin
    83	      depth_q <= '0;
    84	      data_q  <= '0;
    85	      clr_q   <= 1'b1;
    86	    end else begin
    87	      depth_q <= depth_d;
    88	      data_q  <= data_d;
    89	      clr_q   <= clr_d;
    90	    end
    91	  end
    92	
    93	  // flop for handling reset case for clr
    94	  assign clr_d = clr_i;
    95	
    96	  assign depth_o = depth_q;
    97	
    98	  if (InW < OutW) begin : gen_pack_mode
    99	    logic [MaxW-1:0] wdata_shifted;
   100	
   101	    assign wdata_shifted = {{OutW - InW{1'b0}}, wdata_i} << (depth_q*InW);
   102	    assign clear_status = (rready_i && rvalid_o) || clr_q;
   103	    assign clear_data = (ClearOnRead && clear_status) || clr_q;
   104	    assign load_data = wvalid_i && wready_o;
   105	
   106	    assign depth_d =  clear_status ? '0 :
   107	           load_data ? (depth_q + DepthOne):
   108	           depth_q;
   109	
   110	    assign data_d = clear_data ? '0 :
   111	           load_data ? (wdata_shifted | (depth_q == 0 ? '0 : data_q)) :
   112	           data_q;
   113	
   114	    // set outputs
   115	    assign wready_o = !(depth_q == FullDepth) && !clr_q;
   116	    assign rdata_o =  data_q;
   117	    assign rvalid_o = (depth_q == FullDepth) && !clr_q;
   118	
   119	  end else begin : gen_unpack_mode
   120	    logic [MaxW-1:0] rdata_shifted;
   121	    logic            pull_data;
   122	    logic [DepthW:0] ptr_q, ptr_d;
   123	    logic [DepthW:0] lsb_is_one;
   124	    logic [DepthW:0] max_value;
   125	
   126	    always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
   127	      if (!rst_ni) begin
   128	        ptr_q   <= '0;
   129	      end else begin
   130	        ptr_q   <= ptr_d;
   131	      end
   132	    end
   133	
   134	    assign lsb_is_one = {{DepthW{1'b0}},1'b1};
   135	    assign max_value = FullDepth;

   137	    assign clear_status = (rready_i && (depth_q == lsb_is_one)) || clr_q;
   138	    assign clear_data = (ClearOnRead && clear_status) || clr_q;
   139	    assign load_data = wvalid_i && wready_o;
   140	    assign pull_data = rvalid_o && rready_i;
   141	
   142	    assign depth_d =  clear_status ? '0 :
   143	           load_data ? max_value :
   144	           pull_data ? (depth_q - DepthOne) :
   145	           depth_q;
   146	
   147	    assign ptr_d =  clear_status ? '0 :
   148	           pull_data ? (ptr_q + DepthOne) :
   149	           ptr_q;
   150	
   151	    assign data_d = clear_data ? '0 :
   152	           load_data ? wdata_i :
   153	           data_q;
   154	
   155	    // set outputs
   156	    assign wready_o = (depth_q == '0) && !clr_q;
   157	    assign rdata_o =  rdata_shifted[OutW-1:0];
   158	    assign rvalid_o = !(depth_q == '0) && !clr_q;
   159	
   160	    // Avoid possible lint errors in case InW > OutW.
   161	    if (InW > OutW) begin : gen_unused
   162	      logic [MaxW-MinW-1:0] unused_rdata_shifted;
   163	      assign unused_rdata_shifted = rdata_shifted[MaxW-1:MinW];
   164	    end
   165	  end
   166	
   167	
   168	  //////////////////////////////////////////////
   169	  // Assertions, Assumptions, and Coverpoints //
   170	  //////////////////////////////////////////////
   171	
   172	  // If not acked, valid_o should keep asserting
   173	  `ASSERT(ValidOPairedWithReadyI_A,
   174	          rvalid_o && !rready_i && !clr_i |=> rvalid_o)
   175	
   176	  // If output port doesn't accept the data, the data should be stable
   177	  `ASSERT(DataOStableWhenPending_A,
   178	          ##1 rvalid_o && $past(rvalid_o)
   179	          && !$past(rready_i) && !$past(clr_i) |-> $stable(rdata_o))
   180	
   181	endmodule

-- Running command `help equiv_make; help equiv_simple; help equiv_induct; help sat' --

    equiv_make [options] gold_module gate_module equiv_module

This creates a module annotated with $equiv cells from two presumably
equivalent modules. Use commands such as 'equiv_simple' and 'equiv_status'
to work with the created equivalent checking module.

    -inames
        Also match cells and wires with $... names.

    -blacklist <file>
        Do not match cells or signals that match the names in the file.

    -encfile <file>
        Match FSM encodings using the description from the file.
        See 'help fsm_recode' for details.

    -make_assert
        Check equivalence with $assert cells instead of $equiv.
        $eqx (===) is used to compare signals.
Note: The circuit created by this command is not a miter (with something like
a trigger output), but instead uses $equiv cells to encode the equivalence
checking problem. Use 'miter -equiv' if you want to create a miter circuit.


    equiv_simple [options] [selection]

This command tries to prove $equiv cells using a simple direct SAT approach.

    -undef
        enable modelling of undef states

    -seq <N>
        the max. number of time steps to be considered (default = 1)

    -set-assumes
        set all assumptions provided via $assume cells

    -ignore-unknown-cells
        ignore all cells that can not be matched to a SAT model
    -v
        verbose output

    -short
        create shorter input cones that stop at shared nodes. This yields
        simpler SAT problems but sometimes fails to prove equivalence.

    -nogroup
        disabling grouping of $equiv cells by output wire



    equiv_induct [options] [selection]

Uses a version of temporal induction to prove $equiv cells.

Only selected $equiv cells are proven and only selected cells are used to
perform the proof.

    -undef
        enable modelling of undef states

    -seq <N>
        the max. number of time steps to be considered (default = 4)

    -set-assumes
        set all assumptions provided via $assume cells

    -ignore-unknown-cells
        ignore all cells that can not be matched to a SAT model

This command is very effective in proving complex sequential circuits, when
the internal state of the circuit quickly propagates to $equiv cells.

However, this command uses a weak definition of 'equivalence': This command
proves that the two circuits will not diverge after they produce equal
outputs (observable points via $equiv) for at least <N> cycles (the <N>
specified via -seq).

Combined with simulation this is very powerful because simulation can give
you confidence that the circuits start out synced for at least <N> cycles
after reset.


    sat [options] [selection]

This command solves a SAT problem defined over the currently selected circuit
and additional constraints passed as parameters.

    -all
        show all solutions to the problem (this can grow exponentially, use
        -max <N> instead to get <N> solutions)

    -max <N>
        like -all, but limit number of solutions to <N>

    -enable_undef
        enable modeling of undef value (aka 'x-bits')
        this option is implied by -set-def, -set-undef et. cetera

    -max_undef
        maximize the number of undef bits in solutions, giving a better
        picture of which input bits are actually vital to the solution.

    -set <signal> <value>
        set the specified signal to the specified value.

    -set-def <signal>
        add a constraint that all bits of the given signal must be defined

    -set-any-undef <signal>
        add a constraint that at least one bit of the given signal is undefined

    -set-all-undef <signal>
        add a constraint that all bits of the given signal are undefined

    -set-def-inputs
        add -set-def constraints for all module inputs

    -set-def-formal
        add -set-def constraints for formal $anyinit, $anyconst, $anyseq cells

    -show <signal>
        show the model for the specified signal. if no -show option is
        passed then a set of signals to be shown is automatically selected.

    -show-inputs, -show-outputs, -show-ports
        add all module (input/output) ports to the list of shown signals

    -show-regs, -show-public, -show-all
        show all registers, show signals with 'public' names, show all signals

    -ignore-div-by-zero
        ignore all solutions that involve a division by zero

    -ignore-unknown-cells
        ignore all cells that can not be matched to a SAT model

The following options can be used to set up a sequential problem:

    -seq <N>
        set up a sequential problem with <N> time steps. The steps will
        be numbered from 1 to N.

        note: for large <N> it can be significantly faster to use
        -tempinduct-baseonly -maxsteps <N> instead of -seq <N>.

    -set-at <N> <signal> <value>
    -unset-at <N> <signal>
        set or unset the specified signal to the specified value in the
        given timestep. this has priority over a -set for the same signal.

    -set-assumes
        set all assumptions provided via $assume cells

    -set-def-at <N> <signal>
    -set-any-undef-at <N> <signal>
    -set-all-undef-at <N> <signal>
        add undef constraints in the given timestep.

    -set-init <signal> <value>
        set the initial value for the register driving the signal to the value

    -set-init-undef
        set all initial states (not set using -set-init) to undef

    -set-init-def
        do not force a value for the initial state but do not allow undef

    -set-init-zero
        set all initial states (not set using -set-init) to zero

    -dump_vcd <vcd-file-name>
        dump SAT model (counter example in proof) to VCD file

    -dump_json <json-file-name>
        dump SAT model (counter example in proof) to a WaveJSON file.

    -dump_cnf <cnf-file-name>
        dump CNF of SAT problem (in DIMACS format). in temporal induction
        proofs this is the CNF of the first induction step.

The following additional options can be used to set up a proof. If also -seq
is passed, a temporal induction proof is performed.

    -tempinduct
        Perform a temporal induction proof. In a temporal induction proof it is
        proven that the condition holds forever after the number of time steps
        specified using -seq.

    -tempinduct-def
        Perform a temporal induction proof. Assume an initial state with all
        registers set to defined values for the induction step.

    -tempinduct-baseonly
        Run only the basecase half of temporal induction (requires -maxsteps)

    -tempinduct-inductonly
        Run only the induction half of temporal induction

    -tempinduct-skip <N>
        Skip the first <N> steps of the induction proof.

        note: this will assume that the base case holds for <N> steps.
        this must be proven independently with "-tempinduct-baseonly
        -maxsteps <N>". Use -initsteps if you just want to set a
        minimal induction length.

    -prove <signal> <value>
        Attempt to proof that <signal> is always <value>.

    -prove-x <signal> <value>
        Like -prove, but an undef (x) bit in the lhs matches any value on
        the right hand side. Useful for equivalence checking.

    -prove-asserts
        Prove that all asserts in the design hold.

     4	//
     5	// Hardened counter primitive:
     6	//
     7	// This internally uses a cross counter scheme with primary and a secondary counter, where the
     8	// secondary counter counts in reverse direction. The sum of both counters must remain constant and
     9	// equal to 2**Width-1 or otherwise an err_o will be asserted.
    10	//
    11	// This counter supports a generic clear / set / increment / decrement interface:
    12	//
    13	// clr_i: This clears the primary counter to ResetValue and adjusts the secondary counter to match
    14	//        (i.e. 2**Width-1-ResetValue). Clear has priority over set, increment and decrement.
    15	// set_i: This sets the primary counter to set_cnt_i and adjusts the secondary counter to match
    16	//        (i.e. 2**Width-1-set_cnt_i). Set has priority over increment and decrement.
    17	// incr_en_i: Increments the primary counter by step_i, and decrements the secondary by step_i.
    18	// decr_en_i: Decrements the primary counter by step_i, and increments the secondary by step_i.
    19	// commit_i: Counter changes only take effect when `commit_i` is set. This does not effect the
    20	//           `cnt_after_commit_o` output which gives the next counter state if the change is
    21	//           committed.
    22	//
    23	// Note that if both incr_en_i and decr_en_i are asserted at the same time, the counter remains
    24	// unchanged. The counter is also protected against under- and overflows.
    25	
    26	`include "prim_assert.sv"
    27	
    28	module prim_count
    29	  import prim_count_pkg::*;
    30	#(
    31	  parameter int               Width = 2,
    32	  // Can be used to reset the counter to a different value than 0, for example when
    33	  // the counter is used as a down-counter.
    34	  parameter logic [Width-1:0] ResetValue = '0,
    35	  // This should only be disabled in special circumstances, for example
    36	  // in non-comportable IPs where an error does not trigger an alert.
    37	  parameter bit               EnableAlertTriggerSVA = 1,
    38	
    39	  // We have some assertions below with preconditions that depend on particular input actions
    40	  // (clear, set, incr, decr). If the design has instantiated prim_count with one of these actions
    41	  // tied to zero, the preconditions for the associated assertions will not be satisfiable. The
    42	  // result is an unreachable item, which we treat as a failed assertion in the report.
    43	  //
    44	  // To avoid this, we the instantiation to specify the actions which might happen. If this is not
    45	  // '1, we will have an assertion which assert the corresponding action is never triggered. We can
    46	  // then use this to avoid the unreachable assertions.
    47	  parameter action_mask_t     PossibleActions = {$bits(action_mask_t){1'b1}}
    48	) (
    49	  input clk_i,
    50	  input rst_ni,
    51	  input clr_i,
    52	  input set_i,
    53	  input [Width-1:0] set_cnt_i,                 // Set value for the counter.
    54	  input incr_en_i,
    55	  input decr_en_i,
    56	  input [Width-1:0] step_i,                    // Increment/decrement step when enabled.
    57	  input commit_i,
    58	  output logic [Width-1:0] cnt_o,              // Current counter state
    59	  output logic [Width-1:0] cnt_after_commit_o, // Next counter state if committed
    60	  output logic err_o
    61	);
    62	
    63	  ///////////////////
    64	  // Counter logic //
    65	  ///////////////////
    66	
    67	  // Reset Values for primary and secondary counters.
    68	  localparam int NumCnt = 2;
    69	  localparam logic [NumCnt-1:0][Width-1:0] ResetValues = {{Width{1'b1}} - ResetValue, // secondary
    70	                                                          ResetValue};                // primary
    71	
    72	  logic [NumCnt-1:0][Width-1:0] cnt_d, cnt_d_committed, cnt_q;
    73	
    74	  // The fpv_force signal can be used in FPV runs to make the internal counters (cnt_q) jump
    75	  // unexpectedly. We only want to use this mechanism when we're doing FPV on prim_count itself. In
    76	  // that situation, we will have the PrimCountFpv define and wish to leave fpv_force undriven so
    77	  // that it becomes a free variable in FPV. In any other situation, we drive the signal with zero.
    78	  logic [NumCnt-1:0][Width-1:0] fpv_force;
    79	`ifndef PrimCountFpv
    80	  assign fpv_force = '0;
    81	`endif
    82	
    83	  for (genvar k = 0; k < NumCnt; k++) begin : gen_cnts
    84	    // Note that increments / decrements are reversed for the secondary counter.
    85	    logic incr_en, decr_en;
    86	    logic [Width-1:0] set_val;
    87	    if (k == 0) begin : gen_up_cnt
    88	      assign incr_en = incr_en_i;
    89	      assign decr_en = decr_en_i;
    90	      assign set_val = set_cnt_i;
    91	    end else begin : gen_dn_cnt
    92	      assign incr_en = decr_en_i;
    93	      assign decr_en = incr_en_i;
    94	      // The secondary value needs to be adjusted accordingly.
    95	      assign set_val = {Width{1'b1}} - set_cnt_i;
    96	    end
    97	
    98	    // Main counter logic
    99	    logic [Width:0] ext_cnt;
   100	    assign ext_cnt = (decr_en) ? {1'b0, cnt_q[k]} - {1'b0, step_i} :
   101	                     (incr_en) ? {1'b0, cnt_q[k]} + {1'b0, step_i} : {1'b0, cnt_q[k]};
   102	
   103	    // Saturation logic
   104	    logic uflow, oflow;
   105	    assign oflow = incr_en && ext_cnt[Width];
   106	    assign uflow = decr_en && ext_cnt[Width];
   107	    logic [Width-1:0] cnt_sat;
   108	    assign cnt_sat = (uflow) ? '0            :
   109	                     (oflow) ? {Width{1'b1}} : ext_cnt[Width-1:0];
   110	
   111	    // Clock gate flops when in saturation, and do not
   112	    // count if both incr_en and decr_en are asserted.
   113	    logic cnt_en;
   114	    assign cnt_en = (incr_en ^ decr_en) &&
   115	                    ((incr_en && !(&cnt_q[k])) ||
   116	                    (decr_en && !(cnt_q[k] == '0)));
   117	
   118	    // Counter muxes
   119	    assign cnt_d[k] = (clr_i)  ? ResetValues[k] :
   120	                      (set_i)  ? set_val        :
   121	                      (cnt_en) ? cnt_sat        : cnt_q[k];
   122	
   123	    assign cnt_d_committed[k] = commit_i ? cnt_d[k] : cnt_q[k];
   124	
   125	    logic [Width-1:0] cnt_unforced_q;
   126	    prim_flop #(
   127	      .Width(Width),
   128	      .ResetValue(ResetValues[k])
   129	    ) u_cnt_flop (
   130	      .clk_i,
   131	      .rst_ni,
   132	      .d_i(cnt_d_committed[k]),
   133	      .q_o(cnt_unforced_q)
   134	    );
   135	
   136	    // fpv_force is only used during FPV.
   137	    assign cnt_q[k] = fpv_force[k] + cnt_unforced_q;
   138	  end
   139	
   140	  // The sum of both counters must always equal the counter maximum.
   141	  logic [Width:0] sum;
   142	  assign sum = (cnt_q[0] + cnt_q[1]);
   143	
   144	  // Register the error signal to avoid potential CDC issues downstream.
   145	  logic err_d, err_q;
   146	  assign err_d = (sum != {1'b0, {Width{1'b1}}});
   147	  always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
   148	    if (!rst_ni) begin
   149	      err_q <= 1'b0;
   150	    end else begin
   151	      err_q <= err_d;
   152	    end
   153	  end
   154	  assign err_o = err_q;
   155	
   156	  // Output count values
   157	  assign cnt_o              = cnt_q[0];
   158	  assign cnt_after_commit_o = cnt_d[0];
   159	
   160	  ////////////////
   161	  // Assertions //
   162	  ////////////////

   165	  // pragma coverage off
